## Where does a cell come from?

Every cell you have met came from a cell that already existed, by cell division. That reaches back a very long way. The first cells may have formed in water, perhaps in small pools with changing conditions like the hot springs of Puga Valley.

<!-- STEP -->
## How did tools show us a world we cannot see?

Our eyes cannot separate two points closer than about 0.1 mm, and most cells are smaller than that. Light microscopes showed us cells, and electron microscopes showed the parts inside them. Each better tool gave new knowledge.

<!-- STEP -->
## How is the cell the unit of life?

All living organisms are made up of cells, so the cell is the unit of structure. Each cell also carries out the work of life: it takes in materials, releases energy, makes proteins and divides. So it is the unit of function too.

<!-- STEP -->
## How does a cell multiply?

A cell copies its DNA and divides. Mitosis gives two cells with the same chromosomes as the parent, for growth and repair. Meiosis divides twice and gives four cells with half the number, for making gametes.
